proposal.title: RFC 2119 requirement strength: MUST / SHOULD / MAY (+ NOT)

items.english: The specification discusses validating the server certificate.
items.ainglish: The specification says clients MUST validate the server certificate.
items.question: Does the specification make certificate validation an absolute requirement?

items.english: The specification mentions response compression.
items.ainglish: The specification says servers SHOULD compress large responses.
items.question: Does the specification recommend compressing large responses?

items.english: The specification covers a dry-run mode.
items.ainglish: The specification says implementations MAY offer a dry-run mode.
items.question: Does the specification make dry-run mode optional?

items.english: The specification talks about session tokens and logging.
items.ainglish: The specification says loggers MUST NOT record session tokens.
items.question: Does the specification prohibit recording session tokens?

items.english: The server is required to log every authentication failure; this is an absolute requirement of the specification and no circumstances excuse skipping it.
items.ainglish: The server MUST log every authentication failure.
items.question: A server skips this behaviour but documents a considered reason. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Clients are required to send the request identifier on every retry; the specification permits no exception to this.
items.ainglish: Clients MUST send the request identifier on every retry.
items.question: A client omits this behaviour after weighing the trade-offs. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: The proxy is required to strip hop-by-hop headers before forwarding; implementations have no discretion here.
items.ainglish: The proxy MUST strip hop-by-hop headers before forwarding.
items.question: A proxy does not do this, and explains why in its documentation. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Resolvers are required to validate the response signature; this requirement is unconditional.
items.ainglish: Resolvers MUST validate the response signature.
items.question: A resolver skips this step for performance and says so plainly. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is recommended that the client retry with exponential backoff; there can exist valid reasons to do otherwise, provided the implications are understood and carefully weighed.
items.ainglish: The client SHOULD retry with exponential backoff.
items.question: A client deviates from this behaviour after understanding and weighing the implications. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is recommended that servers compress responses larger than one kilobyte, though an implementation aware of the consequences can choose not to in particular circumstances.
items.ainglish: Servers SHOULD compress responses larger than one kilobyte.
items.question: A server does not do this, having examined and accepted the consequences. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is recommended that the gateway cache successful lookups for one hour; deviating is acceptable when the full implications have been considered.
items.ainglish: The gateway SHOULD cache successful lookups for one hour.
items.question: A gateway deviates from this behaviour with a documented, considered rationale. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is recommended that agents announce protocol version on connect; an implementation can omit this in particular circumstances if the trade-off is understood.
items.ainglish: Agents SHOULD announce protocol version on connect.
items.question: An agent omits this after careful consideration of the trade-off. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Implementations are free to offer a dry-run mode; this is genuinely optional and omitting it is equally acceptable.
items.ainglish: Implementations MAY offer a dry-run mode.
items.question: An implementation does not provide this at all. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: The scheduler can optionally coalesce adjacent jobs; providing or not providing this is entirely at the implementer's discretion.
items.ainglish: The scheduler MAY coalesce adjacent jobs.
items.question: A scheduler never does this. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: A registry is permitted, at its own discretion, to serve stale reads during failover; either choice is acceptable.
items.ainglish: A registry MAY serve stale reads during failover.
items.question: A registry chooses never to do this. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Clients can optionally pin the intermediate certificate; the choice carries no conformance weight either way.
items.ainglish: Clients MAY pin the intermediate certificate.
items.question: A client does not do this. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: The relay is absolutely prohibited from forwarding credentials to third parties; no circumstance makes this acceptable.
items.ainglish: The relay MUST NOT forward credentials to third parties.
items.question: A relay does this once, with the user's consent and a documented reason. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Loggers are absolutely prohibited from recording session tokens; the specification admits no exception.
items.ainglish: Loggers MUST NOT record session tokens.
items.question: A logger records them briefly during debugging, with access controls. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: The client is absolutely prohibited from downgrading to plaintext after a failed handshake; there is no permitted exception.
items.ainglish: The client MUST NOT downgrade to plaintext after a failed handshake.
items.question: A client downgrades when the operator explicitly requests it. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: Mirrors are absolutely prohibited from rewriting artifact digests; no operational need excuses it.
items.ainglish: Mirrors MUST NOT rewrite artifact digests.
items.question: A mirror rewrites one digest to fix a known corruption, and discloses this. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is discouraged for services to hold connections open past sixty seconds, though there can exist valid reasons to do so in particular circumstances when the implications are understood and weighed.
items.ainglish: Services SHOULD NOT hold connections open past sixty seconds.
items.question: A service does this for one long-lived subscription, having weighed the implications. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is discouraged for exporters to inline large payloads, but an implementation that has understood and accepted the implications can do so in particular cases.
items.ainglish: Exporters SHOULD NOT inline large payloads.
items.question: An exporter inlines one payload after considering the implications carefully. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is discouraged for agents to poll more than once per minute; doing so is acceptable only in particular circumstances where the full implications are understood.
items.ainglish: Agents SHOULD NOT poll more than once per minute.
items.question: An agent polls faster during a declared incident, having weighed the implications. Per this instruction it is:

items.english: It is discouraged for builds to fetch dependencies at run time, though a valid, carefully weighed reason can make it acceptable in a particular circumstance.
items.ainglish: Builds SHOULD NOT fetch dependencies at run time.
items.question: A build fetches one dependency at run time for a documented, weighed reason. Per this instruction it is:
